previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with worsening shortness of breath due to progressive tracheal and left main bronchial stenosis related to relapsing polychondritis. He underwent bronchoscopy with balloon dilation of the trachea and left main bronchus, which improved airway patency. Post-procedure, he required brief ventilation and norepinephrine for sedation-related hypotension, both quickly weaned. He was treated with intravenous solumedrol, transitioned to a prednisone taper, and maintained on his home medications including methotrexate and etanercept. His elevated white count and lactate normalized, and chest imaging showed improvement in lung opacities. He remained stable, ambulatory, and was discharged home with follow-up arranged with rheumatology, pulmonology, and primary care.
